premises.statement: The staged project table contains a team_name column.
premises.evidence_of_dependence: SELECT p.team_id,p.team_name ... FROM staging.stg_asana__project p ... GROUP BY p.team_id,p.team_name
premises.alternative: The stg_asana__project contract lists team_id but no team_name; team_name is supplied by staging.stg_asana__team.
premises.reason: The project aggregation cannot execute if the referenced column is absent.

premises.statement: Joining assigned task rows to the user directory would produce no matched users for any team.
premises.alternative: The contract requires users linked by assignee_user_id=user_id, defaults their grade to 'developing_performer' and portfolio_task_count to 0, and counts distributions across joined task rows.
premises.reason: Omitting the user join replaces required task-weighted member distributions and averages with constants.

premises.statement: Both collaboration_efficiency_score and resource_optimization_score are zero for every team.
premises.alternative: The contract requires these scores to be calculated from performer, workload, and risk shares when unique_team_members is positive.
premises.reason: Hardcoding both components can materially change overall efficiency scores and downstream classifications.

premises.statement: Every team passing the implemented identifier and count checks also has avg_completion_rate and avg_quality_rate within the required non-null range of 0 through 100.
premises.evidence_of_dependence: (t.team_id IS NOT NULL AND t.team_name IS NOT NULL AND COALESCE(ps.total_projects,0)>=0 ... ) is_valid_record
premises.alternative: The contract requires avg_completion_rate and avg_quality_rate to be within [0,100] and says averages are NULL when no health values exist.
premises.reason: Teams without qualifying project health data can be retained despite failing the specified validation.

premises.statement: Project-size distribution in team efficiency metrics should be inferred from task-count bands rather than defaulted to medium_project.
premises.evidence_of_dependence: COUNT(*) FILTER(WHERE h.total_tasks>100) enterprise_projects ... COUNT(*) FILTER(WHERE h.total_tasks BETWEEN 21 AND 50) medium_projects
premises.alternative: The contract specifies 'project_health_summary: project health fields with project_size_category defaulted to medium_project'.
premises.reason: The inferred bands redistribute projects across size categories instead of applying the documented default.

premises.statement: Time-management scoring may be based on completion and deadline status instead of schedule_forecast.
premises.evidence_of_dependence: CASE WHEN completion_percentage=100 THEN 25 WHEN remaining_days<0 THEN 5 ELSE 12 END time_management_score
premises.alternative: The contract maps schedule_forecast to scores: 'on_schedule 25; slight_delay 20; moderate_delay 15; significant_delay 10; overdue 5; else 12'.
premises.reason: This substitution changes the time score, comprehensive score, and performance ranks.

premises.statement: No project entering project analytics has a negative elapsed_days value.
premises.alternative: The contract requires completion_rate_per_day to be NULL 'if elapsed_days is not positive', whereas NULLIF only handles zero.
premises.reason: Future-created projects would receive negative completion rates instead of NULL.

premises.statement: Every non-null project team_id has a matching staged team.
premises.alternative: The analytics column description says team_id is 'null if no matching team'; selecting p.team_id preserves unmatched identifiers.
premises.reason: Unmatched teams would leave non-null team identifiers where the output contract calls for NULL.

premises.statement: Any task with a non-null completed_at timestamp is completed, even when is_completed is false.
premises.alternative: The contract specifies using completed_at 'if completed, else to the current time'.
premises.reason: An inconsistent open task would have its lifecycle duration and activity-rate denominator stopped at completed_at.

premises.statement: A task missing performance metrics should receive an activity contribution equivalent to activity_score 1 in lifecycle_health_score.
premises.alternative: The contract specifies 'Activity: activity_score*4' without defining a fallback score for missing metrics.
premises.reason: The fallback changes health scores and permits scoring tasks whose performance metrics were excluded upstream.

premises.statement: An assigned open task with a missing modified_at timestamp should be classified as stagnant after failing the newly_assigned condition.
premises.evidence_of_dependence: WHEN NOT is_completed AND assignee_user_id IS NOT NULL THEN 'stagnant'
premises.alternative: The contract requires 'last modification >7 days' for stagnant and provides an 'unknown_state' fallback.
premises.reason: Missing modification timestamps are treated as evidence of staleness rather than an unknown state.

premises.statement: Passing staging task timestamps through unchanged satisfies the lifecycle mart's timezone-aware timestamp requirements.
premises.alternative: Staging declares these fields as TIMESTAMP, while the lifecycle contract declares created_at, completed_at, and due_date as TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE.
premises.reason: The mart inherits timezone-naive types without establishing the contracted timezone-aware types.

premises.statement: An open task without a due_date should receive five timeliness points in lifecycle_health_score.
premises.evidence_of_dependence: WHEN due_date::DATE>CURRENT_DATE THEN 35 WHEN due_date::DATE=CURRENT_DATE THEN 25 ELSE 5 END
premises.alternative: The contract assigns five points for 'overdue' but does not explicitly assign a timeliness contribution to tasks without a due date.
premises.reason: The unspecified missing-deadline treatment affects lifecycle scores and score-based patterns.

fewer.reason: Only three additional unsupported premises were identifiable; other visible logic follows explicit contract rules or depends on premises already recorded.
